solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Stifling regrets, try this compiler: horrible (8)

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so one word is wrapped round another and held inside it

blocks.note: to have a go = to try

annotation.surface: A setter admits their puzzle is so dreadful that solvers will have to choke back their regrets.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'stifling' as an adjective describing the regrets; it is a verb acting on them. Setters often call themselves 'this compiler', 'the setter' or 'yours truly'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: gruesome and horrible both describe something dreadful enough to make you shudder.

entries.clue: Rule covering relative in old school exam (10)

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so these letters go inside the exam's

blocks.note: General Certificate of Education, the old British school exam
over = covering, lying on top of

annotation.surface: A school regulation about which of a pupil's relatives may cover for them in an old exam.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Covering' looks like the container signal, but it only gives a piece; the real signal is the little word 'in'. The GCE was replaced in England by GCSEs in the 1980s.
annotation.definitionFit: Noun synonym: rule in the sense of government or control, which is what governance means.

entries.clue: I don’t like that cough after poisonous gas dropped (3)

indicators.note: something dropped is let fall and lost, so these letters fall out of the word

blocks.note: CO = carbon monoxide, removed from the front

annotation.surface: Someone coughs after a toxic gas is released and complains about it.
annotation.walkthrough: On the surface the gas is dropped into the air; in the wordplay it is dropped out of COUGH. Chemical formulas like CO are fair game in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is a whole spoken phrase, and 'ugh' is the grunt that says exactly that.

entries.clue: Carpet covered in Koranic verses in mainly Muslim island (7)

indicators.note: a thing covered in something is wrapped all round by it, so the carpet sits inside the verses

blocks.note: a sura is a chapter of the Koran
a mat is a small carpet

annotation.surface: A prayer rug embroidered with Koranic verses, in a mostly Muslim island.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface stays in the Islamic world, so the carpet feels like a prayer mat, which is just what it turns out to give.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: Sumatra is an Indonesian island whose people are largely Muslim.

entries.clue: Militancy up, I worked out, in local government area (12)

indicators.note: something worked out has been worked over and reshaped, so the letters are put into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone notices that political militancy is rising in their town council's area.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Worked out' reads as 'figured out', as if the speaker has noticed the rise; it is telling you to rearrange the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain description: a municipality is a town or district run by its own local council.

entries.clue: Being family good for making requests (6)

blocks.note: as = being, as in 'as it was raining'

annotation.surface: Being part of a family is useful when you need favours.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a noun on the surface, but it gives AS, the conjunction meaning 'since'.
annotation.definitionFit: Participle for participle: the definition is a verb phrase in -ing, and one word for putting requests is the matching -ing form.

entries.clue: Punch son, more irate by the sound of it (7)

indicators.note: judging by how it sounds rather than how it is spelt, so you say ANGRIER and write what you hear

blocks.clueFragment: more irate by the sound of it
blocks.note: angrier = more irate, said without sounding the final R

annotation.surface: A parent is urged to hit their son, who apparently is getting angrier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Punch' looks like a verb ordering violence; it is the drink. The sound only matches in accents that drop a final R, as most English ones do.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: sangria, Spanish red wine mixed with fruit, is one kind of punch.

entries.clue: In gentle light at first it may become bright (11)

indicators.note: the first thing you meet in a word is its first letter, so only L is taken
the letters can turn into something new, which is what rearranging them does

annotation.surface: Something seen in soft light at first can grow bright.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Light' and 'bright' keep you thinking of lamps; 'bright' is the definition in its clever sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in its mental sense: a bright child is a clever one.

entries.clue: Sign of aggression in boxer perhaps ultimately failing to develop (4)

indicators.note: what fails ultimately gives out at the very end, so the last letter goes

blocks.clueFragment: Sign of aggression in boxer perhaps
blocks.note: a boxer is a breed of dog, and a dog growls

annotation.surface: A boxer's aggression fades at the end of a fight, and they never mature.
annotation.walkthrough: The boxer is a dog, not a fighter; 'perhaps' flags it as just one example of a dog.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to develop is to grow, as a child or a plant does.

entries.clue: Furious former soldier stopped by well-built guys (8)

indicators.note: a pipe stopped by something has it plugged inside, so these letters sit in the middle of the veteran

annotation.surface: An angry ex-serviceman is blocked by a group of burly men.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'stopped' mean blocked in the street; in the wordplay it means stoppered, filled in the middle.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym: a vehement protest is fierce and passionate, close to furious.

entries.clue: Blows that hurt singer almost making a comeback (3-3)

indicators.note: almost the whole word is nearly all of it, so the last letter is cut
coming back means going the way you came, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: ow! is what you say when something hurts

annotation.surface: A singer who once took painful blows is nearly ready to return to the stage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blows that hurt' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Blows'; 'that hurt' is the cry OW.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a one-two is a pair of quick punches, a left then a right.

entries.clue: Chivalrous man’s dark sin pierces philosopher (6,6)

indicators.note: what pierces something goes right into it, so these letters drive inside the philosopher

annotation.surface: A gallant man's secret wrongdoing wounds a thinker.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay, not a possessive. Kant is the crossword's favourite philosopher because his name splits so easily.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a knight errant was a medieval knight roaming in search of chivalrous deeds.

entries.clue: Unlikely key that is used by surfer (6,7)

blocks.note: a remote chance is an unlikely one
the Control key on a computer keyboard

annotation.surface: An odd keyboard key that a web surfer relies on.
annotation.walkthrough: Keys and surfing point to the internet; the surfer is a channel-surfer flicking through television channels.
annotation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a channel-surfer's essential tool is the remote control.

entries.clue: Make a rule about conserving television’s current worth (6,5)

indicators.note: letters moved about are scattered into a new order
to conserve something is to keep it safe within, so the rearranged letters hold TV

annotation.surface: A regulator makes a rule to protect what television is worth today.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Make a rule' reads as the action of the sentence, but it is the raw letters. The 's on television is 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain description: market value is what something would fetch if sold now, its current worth.

entries.clue: Confirmed louse possibly dismisses R&B (10)

indicators.note: to dismiss someone is to send them away, so R and B are sent out of the word

blocks.note: a louse is one kind of invertebrate

annotation.surface: A confirmed scoundrel might sneer at rhythm and blues music.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Louse' reads as an insult for a person; it is the insect, an example of an invertebrate.
annotation.definitionFit: Synonym in the sense of habit: a confirmed smoker or bachelor is an inveterate one.

entries.clue: With British leaving, abandon a vessel (5)

indicators.note: whoever is leaving goes away, so the B for British departs from the word

annotation.surface: With the British crew gone, orders come to abandon a ship.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'vessel' a ship to be abandoned; it is a blood vessel.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the aorta is the body's main artery, one kind of blood vessel.

entries.clue: Play area patrolled by tiny tailless cat (9)

indicators.note: an area patrolled by guards has them all around it, so A sits inside the other letters
a word's tail is its end, so PYGMY loses its last letter

blocks.note: PYGMY = tiny, without its final Y
a lion is a big cat

annotation.surface: A children's play area is guarded by a small cat with no tail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Play area' reads as a playground; 'Play' alone is the definition, the drama by George Bernard Shaw.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Pygmalion is Shaw's play, later the basis of My Fair Lady.

entries.clue: Check modern car part, finally contact manufacturer (9)

indicators.note: what comes finally is at the end, so only the last letter of 'contact' is used

blocks.note: a part in a play = a role

annotation.surface: A driver inspects a new car's component and then gets in touch with the carmaker.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface is about cars, so 'part' looks like a car part; it is an actor's role.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Chevrolet is an American car manufacturer, part of General Motors.

entries.clue: Echo in two directions in circle (7)

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so the directions go inside the circle

blocks.note: E and S, east and south

annotation.surface: A sound echoes both ways around a circle.
annotation.walkthrough: Any two compass points would fit 'two directions'; only E and S make a word inside ROUND.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: a hall that resounds echoes with noise.

entries.clue: Annoy US deputy, bouncing back with energy (5)

indicators.note: a ball bouncing back returns the way it came, so the word is read backwards

annotation.surface: Someone irritates the American vice-president, who springs back energetically.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bouncing back' reads as recovering from a setback; it only turns VEEP round.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: to peeve someone is to irritate them.

entries.clue: Coloured hock bottles? Too dark now to see (7)

indicators.note: to bottle something is to hold it inside, so the colour sits within the other word

blocks.note: to hock something = to pawn it

annotation.surface: Someone peers at bottles of hock in a cellar too dark to see their colour.
annotation.walkthrough: Hock is a German white wine, and 'bottles' keeps you in the cellar; hock here is the verb, to pawn.
annotation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: the predawn hours are the dark before sunrise, when it is still too dark to see.

entries.clue: Where tourists are welcome, seemingly to take weight off feet (7,6)

blocks.note: the straight reading: a place set up to greet tourists

blocks.clueFragment: seemingly to take weight off feet
blocks.note: the setter's joke: read the answer as 'the centre of VISITOR' and you get SIT

annotation.surface: A welcome spot for tourists where they can rest their feet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Seemingly' flags the second reading: the middle three letters of VISITOR spell SIT, which is to take the weight off your feet.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain description: a visitor centre is where tourists are met with information and a welcome.

entries.clue: Working party ignoring leader of Supreme Court (4)

indicators.note: what you ignore you leave out, so the S is left out of the word
the leader goes at the front, so this is the first letter of 'Supreme'

blocks.note: a squad is a group working together

annotation.surface: A committee disregards the head of the Supreme Court.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supreme Court' looks like one name; it splits, and 'Court' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Noun synonym: a quad, short for quadrangle, is a courtyard enclosed by buildings, as at a college.

entries.clue: Treatment of mutual points changing character’s tone (6)

indicators.note: something given treatment is worked on and altered, so the letters of MUTUAL are reshaped

annotation.surface: Therapy for a couple's shared disagreements changes someone's character and tone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Points' reads as arguments made; they are two dots, and 'character' is a written letter whose sound they alter.
annotation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: an umlaut is the pair of dots over a vowel, as in German ü, that changes its sound.

entries.clue: Steps in Havana hotel a vexation, artist concludes (8)

indicators.note: whatever concludes something comes at its close, so the artist's letters go last

blocks.note: H = hotel in the phonetic alphabet
the bane of one's life is a vexation

annotation.surface: A guest finds the stairs of a Havana hotel a nuisance, an artist decides.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Steps' looks like a staircase; they are dance steps, and 'Havana hotel' reads as one place until you split it.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by origin: the habanera is a slow Cuban dance whose name means 'from Havana'.

entries.clue: Name part of middle name (3)

indicators.note: a part of something is a piece of it, so the answer lies inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: Part of someone's middle name.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Name' appears twice on purpose: the first is the definition, the second supplies the last two letters of the hidden answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Ena is a girl's first name, so it is one name among many.

entries.clue: Daughter understands more than one phobia (6)

blocks.note: to read a situation = to understand it

annotation.surface: A daughter realises someone has several fears.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Understands' gives READS in the sense of reading someone's mood.
annotation.definitionFit: Plural noun synonym: a dread is a deep fear, so several phobias are dreads.

entries.clue: Old time dancing stage one (5,3)

indicators.note: dancers move around each other, so the letters swap places

annotation.surface: The first step in learning old-time ballroom dancing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old time dancing' reads as one phrase, the ballroom style; split after 'time', and 'dancing' becomes the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Stone Age is a prehistoric era, about as old a time as history names.
